result.title: FireGraphNet: Sub-daily wildfire spread prediction with directed graph neural networks
result.summary: Wildfire decisions are made in hours, yet most learned spread models predict daily on targets including burned area. We propose FireGraphNet which formulates 12-hour growth as node classification on directed H3 graphs, with candidates ahead of the front and wind alignment, terrain, fuel continuity and barriers on edges. On satellite perimeters it achieves average precision 1.7-1.9x the strongest distance baseline on test California fires and 1.62x out of state. We show this skill comes from message passing rather than cell features or the aggregator, is highest on young fires in state, is carried deep along the wind by its edges, and is hidden by pooling. A convolutional network matches this ranking once trained on new growth, at worse calibration, so candidate construction, target definition, and aggregation shape conclusions about model skill. Editing fuel and barrier attributes reduces predicted spread more under guided than random placement, extending FireGraphNet to operational intervention analysis.

AI.brief_summary: FireGraphNet 将 12 小时野火蔓延建模为有向 H3 图上的节点分类，边特征编码风向、地形、燃料连续性与屏障，在卫星火烧边界数据上优于距离基线，并做了消融与燃料属性干预分析。
AI.relevance_reason: 这是地理时空预测任务，虽用了有向图消息传递与消融分析，但对象是物理蔓延而非模型内部推理状态，未涉及视觉证据筛选、latent 状态生成或停止决策，找不到可供核查的 LVR 借鉴线索。
